dataset_title: Filtered perennial ryegrass press-juice composition for fermentation-medium characterization
source_title: Short-term adaptation as a tool to improve bioethanol production using grass press-juice as fermentation medium
authors: Ludovica Varriale; Doris Geib; Roland Ulber
source_table_caption: Press-juice composition from the perennial ryegrass Lolium perenne

study_context.processing_scale: Laboratory characterization of press-juice used as a fermentation medium
study_context.material_state: Press-juice centrifuged twice at 4500 rpm for 20 min, paper-filtered, then sterile-filtered at 0.2 micrometre and frozen at -20 C before use

applicability: Reference measurements for the filtered press-juice material state and its use as a fermentation medium. Supports literature comparison and future technology-specific substrate characterization only; it is not a raw-grass profile, not a GreenHub batch, and not an active process default.
limitations: The source material is cultivated perennial ryegrass press-juice, not Dutch roadside grass or the VARTA whole-grass sample.

The composition table does not provide a matched raw-feed sample, juice yield, density, dry matter, or paired press-cake composition, so concentrations cannot be converted to raw-feed mass fractions or a press recovery.
Table 1 does not state replicate count or uncertainty for composition values; do not assign an invented standard deviation.
Reported totals overlap named sugars and ions and must not be added to their constituent rows.
Nitrite is left-censored at less than 0.01 g/L; the numeric value is missing and is not zero.
The reported total protein assay and free-amino-acid assay have different methods and sample preparation; they are analytical properties, not mutually exclusive mass-closure components.
metadata_gaps: Cultivar and harvest date are not specified in this article's material description.
No raw-grass/juice/cake matched mass balance or juice yield is reported here.
No juice density, dry matter, or composition uncertainty for Table 1 is reported.
No mapping to GreenHub's UI feed-component masses is valid without material-state and basis data.
